info.band: Work epics per stage, and per spec phase at the earliest phase of their bound specs; with no graph the phases count task files. From the summary's band. Click a stage to dim every other epic on the graph, again to clear; click a phase to open Specs at it. Milestones: each one open or closed by its opening order with what it waits on, its gate's members done out of members (deferrable members in neither count), and one line: its gate's purpose when it has one, else its threshold as written, absent, a placeholder or met, from the export's milestones. A card opens its milestone in the drawer, with the threshold and the purpose in full.
info.share: Work epics done over all work epics; condition epics are in no figure. From the summary's plan, the share tp epic status reports.
info.ready: Work epics that can start now: open milestone, every dependency done, no bound spec, no claim. In tp epic ready's order, most downstream first.
info.critical: Not-done epics on the longest dependency chain of the whole graph: tp epic status's top-level critical_path.
info.blocked: Work epics waiting on a dependency that is not done. Held epics are the blocked ones a condition holds.
info.held: Blocked work epics a condition epic, or a group of conditions, holds: they wait on an operator decision, not on work.
info.operator: Decisions only the operator takes, each with the command that settles it: actionable conditions (tp epic done), any-of groups of conditions to choose one of, gates whose written threshold awaits --met, placeholder thresholds to rewrite (tp epic set), slices at their cap that can take one more round (tp epic review --grant-round), and the escalations stopping a spec bound to an epic. From the summary's plan, the export's milestones[].operator and slices, and the task file list's escalations.
info.loops: Epic review slices not done, less those a re-review alone settles. What each needs differs: an open or unreviewed slice a round, a stale one with a blocking finding open a round that reads it, one with a round in flight that round recorded, not a new one, one at its cap its findings dispositioned, and one stale at its cap the operator's grant, so it is in the operator queue too. After the plus, the slices a re-review alone settles: a graph edit changed their units since their last round, they would otherwise be done, and they are under their cap. From the summary's open_loops and stale_loops.
info.lint: The error and warning counts tp epic lint prints for the graph, from the export's lint.
info.throughput: Work epics done per ISO week across every milestone, from their done time. From the summary's plan.
info.waiting: What is blocked, and by what. The blocked work epics of open milestones, grouped under each dependency they wait on directly, an any-of group as one: an epic waiting on three blockers is in three groups, so the group sizes do not add up to the total. Each group names its blocker, what the blocker is doing (startable; claimed, specced or in progress, its status as the Lifecycle counts it; an operator decision; or waiting itself) and how many epics wait on it directly. The groups sit in one section per blocker's milestone, in the order the graph file lists the milestones, track by track, an any-of group under its earliest member's; inside a section the largest come first, a few show and the rest are behind the section's own Show all, and a section header folds it. A blocker on the critical path carries a mark; it does not change the order. The blocked epics of milestones not yet open are one counted row, and deferrable gate members are left out, so the parts add up to the blocked epics figure. From the summary's waiting list and the export's blocked_by and blocked_by_any_of.
info.most: Not-done work epics other work epics depend on, transitively, most dependents first.
info.since: What changed since this browser last saw the page: tasks closed and review, audit and plan review rounds recorded, and epics whose stage changed, counted and never named. This browser keeps the last state it saw and compares it on each load; tp stores nothing for it, and a private window or cleared storage shows no strip.
info.cfd: Work epics per stage per day, from the times tp records: claimed at the claim, specced at the earliest binding time of the bound specs, in progress at the earliest start of their tasks, done at the done record or the audit that released the last bound spec. An epic that reached a stage at a time tp did not record (a spec bound before tp recorded binding times) is counted as time not recorded, never on a guessed day. An epic's planning time is not recorded, so an epic added to the graph later counts as planned from the chart's first day. Planned epics are left out of the bands. From the summary's series.
slices.none_html: No slice of the plan has been reviewed: tp epic review --milestone <m> starts one.
info.slices: One row per epic review slice (tp epic review): its round with the cap and the grants spent, its state, the units changed since its last recorded round when it is stale, its open findings by role, and the findings of each recorded round as a curve. From the export's slices and the summary's per-round counts.

info.history: A slice's rounds in order, from tp epic review <slice> --history: each round's findings by role, and what changed in the slice's units since the round before, read from the two rounds' snapshots. A change made and undone between two rounds leaves no trace, and which write made a change is not recorded.
diff.nothing: Nothing changed between these two snapshots.
diff.head.unitsChanged: Units changed (their blocks were not kept, so only which changed is known)
info.graph: The plan as tp lays it out at /api/layout, drawn on one canvas. Plan: every epic, layers top to bottom by what they wait on, each milestone a band, tracks side by side. Each epic sits under one primary parent: its dependency on the critical path when it has one, else its deepest earlier dependency in its track. The path is counted with every epic open, so finishing epics never moves the map; it can cross tracks. Those tree edges are drawn; the other edges into an epic (cross edges) only with Cross edges or K, a back edge (a cycle) in violet, and the critical path in orange whatever its class. Milestones: each milestone with its work epics done and its epic edges in, grouped by track and joined by its opens-after edges, those from another track drawn lighter, K hiding them; click one for its gate's closure. Gate closure: what the milestone's gate pulls in (tp epic scope), banded by milestone, the primary parents taken from its own critical path. Neighbourhood: the selected epic and its dependencies and dependents to the depth picked; it keeps the last epic selected when the drawer closes. Selecting an epic highlights what it waits on in blue and what waits on it in green, fading after two steps unless Show the whole chain is on. The canvas has no focusable epic: the search, the lists, the drawer and the chain as text below carry the keyboard, and on the focused canvas the arrows pan.

info.matrix: Row depends on column: each number counts the dependency edges from the row milestone's epics to the column's, each member of an any-of group one, and its colour says how many of those dependencies are done. The diagonal is the milestone's own share of work epics done. From the summary's matrix and the export's milestones.

drawer.noSpecs: None yet: tp init <spec> --epic {id} binds one.
info.drawer: One epic from tp epic export and the graph: its fields, what it depends on and what depends on it with the whys, downstream (the not-done work epics that wait on it), the specs bound to it with their phase and loops, its stepper (claimed, with who claimed it, or skipped when it was bound unclaimed; bound; done), and its graph history from tp epic review --history --of-epic. A milestone card opens its milestone here instead: its gate's state, its threshold and purpose in full, and how many of its epics are described.
info.ehistory: How this epic's edges and whys read in each recorded round of every epic review slice whose snapshot holds it, from tp epic review --history --of-epic. A round recorded before snapshots kept their text holds hashes only, so it shows no edge or why.
info.specs: Every task file git sees, one row each, from tp export --list: grouped by the phase tp resume reports, in the loop's order (review, decompose, implement, audit, release), the ones an operator decision stops first. Operator decisions shows only those. Click a row to open that spec; press / anywhere to filter.
info.loop: The loop tp runs a spec through: ground its claims, review, decompose into tasks, implement, audit, release. The marked step is the phase tp resume reports; a pause mark there is a decision only the operator takes. Each step's line comes from tp export's loops and tasks.
impact.noEpic: Bound to no epic, so releasing it moves nothing in the plan.
impact.gate_html: brings milestone {ms}'s gate from {from} to {to} of {n} members done
impact.none: Releasing it alone frees no epic and moves no gate.
read.tasksNamed: each section names the tasks written from it
read.tasksLater: tasks are written from these sections after review
read.noSection: The spec has no numbered section.
info.reader: The spec as the file reads now, in its numbered sections, from tp export. Every section and paragraph carries a stable anchor (§3 ¶2; hover a paragraph to see it) that findings and feedback can point at. A section's task count opens Tasks with the tasks written from it picked out.
spechist.none: This spec has recorded no round yet.
spechist.firstRound: The first round: there is no round before to compare with.
spechist.noChange: Nothing changed in the spec since the round before.
info.spechistory: This spec's recorded rounds from tp export: each loop's rounds by the time they were recorded (a ground round records no time, so its file's time stands in), the round table with each round's findings (ground: FAILs) and whether it is clean, with the loop's cap and its current run of clean rounds, and for each review round what changed in the spec since the round before, beside that round's findings.
task.close: Close the task detail and show progress
task.epicWaits_html: Its epic {epic} waits on a dependency, so tp next starts none of this file's tasks yet.
info.tasks: This spec's tasks from tp export, two ways. Steps is the dependency tree: a task sits one step below the last task it waits on, so step 1 needs no other task, and lines join a task to what it waits on. Board is the same tasks by state: ready, in progress, waiting (on a task, or a pause mark when its epic is not ready, so tp next starts none), done; ready and waiting together are tp status's open count. Click a task for its detail, again to show progress.
progress.decomposing: Review is done; decomposing writes the tasks.
progress.inReview: The spec is still in review; its tasks are written once review is done.
progress.clickTask: Click a task for its detail.
progress.goal: all {n} done at the dashed line
info.progress: From the tasks tp export reports: their states, the estimates of the tasks not done, how long each task in progress has run against its estimate, and the closing times as a running count.
